title: 154,000 men went in. Some never left.
caption: Mansfield, Ohio. The Ohio State Reformatory held 154,000 men in 94 years. In 1950 the warden's wife died after a gun fell and fired. Staff believe she never left. slides.text: 154,000 MEN WENT IN. SOME NEVER LEFT.
Mansfield, Ohio. The Ohio State Reformatory. Its cornerstone was laid in 1886.
It looks like a castle on purpose. The architect hoped the building itself would help inmates be 'reborn'.
Inside: the East Cell Block. Six tiers of steel cells, stacked to the ceiling.
At its worst it held around 3,500 men, crammed into cells meant for far fewer.
1950. Helen Glattke, the warden's wife, was in the family's quarters. A handgun fell and fired. She died three days later.
Her husband stayed on as warden. In 1959 he died after a heart attack, still in charge of the prison.
In 1990 a federal court closed it for inhumane conditions. Then Hollywood came: The Shawshank Redemption was filmed here.
Today it's open for tours and ghost hunts. Staff believe Helen still lingers... as a scent that comes from nowhere.
